title: Software modification - Vaporize WCode canonical Pkl resources

featureFlagDisposition.noFlagReason: WCode is already an explicit operator-selected command authority and remains unavailable to existing SwiftPM and Xcode command paths. This change does not make WCode a default or silently select it. A policy-controlled default would require a separate flagged feature request.

stateResults.summary: The operator required canonical Pkl resource declarations and explicitly rejected PowerShell as WCode lifecycle infrastructure.

The Vaporize boundary already contained the admitted Windows Swift path-survival behavior. WCode composition preserves that behavior, and the explicit candidate review found no unrelated tracked deletion or nested repository boundary.

WCode now resolves canonical project.pkl intent, builds through SwiftPM, stages resources and runtime artifacts through typed Swift services, and runs or installs the exact executable without a script callback.

The hardened WCode lifecycle suite passed 8 of 8 tests and the complete WCode-focused selection passed 15 tests on Windows. The tests cover exact runtime closure, path confinement, bounded force reinstall, reserved lifecycle environment keys, and compatible typed receipt emission. With the already-installed WinGet Pkl directory added only to the test process PATH, Vaporize's existing CUJ-14 generated a real .xcodeproj world state and project.pbxproj from XcodeProjectDefinition Pkl. Native xcodebuild remains a macOS release-lane check.
The exact WCode feature files are green and ready for explicit-file persistence.

receiptRefs.t: Vaporize macOS Xcode project generation CUJ

notes: PowerShell remains a possible guest shell selected by a terminal profile; that is outside this lifecycle contract.
Package.swift continues to own compiler-visible Bundle.module resources.
